study_identification_part.si4_title: Mapping the Heterogeneous Brain Structural Phenotype of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using the Normative Model

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Combine NMF with normative modeling to quantify individual-level deviations in gray matter structure in ASD relative to typical development and assess whether deviation patterns identify ASD subtypes with distinct clinical features.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Gaussian mixture clustering on ASD deviation matrix identified 3 subtypes; group comparisons (two-sample t-tests, FDR-corrected) showed subtype differences in ADOS communication (p=0.002) and social (p=0.002) scores; no significant differences in RRB.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: ASD exhibits heterogeneous, individualized deviation patterns in gray matter factor weights; three neuroanatomical subtypes show distinct deviation directions and differences in social/communication symptoms.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: NMF on ABIDE II TD (n=564) yielded six GMV factors; GPR-based normative models (age, gender) produced per-factor W-scores for ABIDE I. ASD showed increased weights/deviations in 5/6 factors versus TD. Gaussian mixture clustering of ABIDE I ASD deviations identified three subtypes: subtypes 1 and 3 with uniformly positive deviations (subtype 3 larger), subtype 2 with uniformly negative deviations. Across subtypes, ADOS Communication differed (p=0.002) and ADOS Social differed (p=0.002) after FDR correction; RRB did not differ (p=0.213).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Integrated NMF with normative modeling to create individualized deviation metrics; used NeuroSynth to decode factor functions; applied Gaussian mixture clustering to deviations to derive ASD subtypes.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Normative models included only age and gender; additional covariates (e.g., cognitive/home environment) may affect brain indices. Despite robust clustering, no brain-symptom correlations were found within/across subtypes; relationships may be complex and non-linear. Multimodal data (rs-fMRI, DTI, genetics) are needed to further parse heterogeneity.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: ABIDE I/II T1 data underwent CAT12/SPM VBM with DPABI GM mask and 10 mm smoothing. QC: three-rater visual scoring (1–5), exclude average<3. Site handled via post-hoc GLM regression (no ComBat/HBR). Software: MATLAB R2015b, GPy, scikit-learn. Supplement reports final ABIDE I counts for complete phenotypes (TD 515; ASD 452).
